Landlords reasonably counter that a credit score is one of the few objective, verifiable signals available quickly during screening, and that removing it entirely leaves them with far less reliable information about financial risk.

Weighing a broader financial picture, including rental history and income stability, rather than a credit score alone, would likely serve both fair access and legitimate landlord caution better than either extreme.
